newsitem.title: USA: Sodak in gaming agreement in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Sodak in gaming agreement in Brazil.

text.p: Sodak Gaming Inc said Tuesday it entered into an agreement with the Brazil Soccer Federation (CBF) to operate video gaming machines in Brazil.
The operations are subject to authorization of individual states, which have regulatory control over such gaming.
Under the exclusive agreement, Sodak will provide equipment and operate the gaming machines on behalf of CBF.

For managing and operating the systems, Sodak is entitled to 44 percent of the system's defined net win. For the development and administration of the linked accounting system and the multi-machine jackpot, Sodak is to receive three percent of the amount of money spent in the machines.
Sodak said the agreement is for eight years and includes a renewal clause.

Under Brazilian law, non-profit organizations can run gaming operations to raise money if the individual states approve, Sodak said. CBF is the governing body for both amateur and professional soccer leagues in Brazil. Sodak said CBF's profits will be used for athletic teams and social programs.
Both Sodak and the CBF said there is a potential for thousands of machines throughout Brazil. They will initiallly seek approval in Rio de Janeiro and Sao Paulo.
